explain.say: Here is something amazing: you learned a whole language before you could tie your shoes, and nobody gave you a single grammar lesson! Look at the timeline on the board. It starts at birth, with crying. That is a baby's first way to say, I need something!

explain.say: Look at the next two stops. At about 2 months babies coo, soft sounds like ooh and aah. At about 6 months they babble: ba-ba, da-da, ma-ma. Babbling is like practice for the mouth. Have you heard a baby babble?

explain.say: Now look at the first words stop, about 12 months. Words like mama, ball and more. Look at the board: ma, ma. Lips together, then an open mouth, are some of the easiest sounds to make. That is why words like mama turn up in so many languages!

explain.say: Back to the timeline. See the word burst at about 18 months? Toddlers can learn new words almost every day. Then at about 2 years come two-word sentences: more milk, daddy go. What do you think your first words were?

explain.say: Well done! Look at the last stop: by 3 to 4 years, children use full sentences and ask a million questions. Wow: babies are born able to hear the sounds of every language, and they slowly tune in to the ones around them. Challenge: ask your family what your first word was!

faq.a: Babbling is when a baby repeats sounds like ba-ba or da-da, usually from about 6 months. It is practice for the mouth and ears, and it starts to sound like the language around them.

faq.q: When do babies say their first word?
faq.a: Most babies say their first real word around their first birthday, but anywhere from about 10 to 15 months is normal. Every child is different.
They hear thousands of sentences and find the patterns themselves. That is why toddlers say goed: they have found the add ed rule and use it everywhere.
asks: How do children learn to talk without lessons?

faq.q: Why is mama a first word in so many languages?
faq.a: Ma and pa use easy sounds: lips together, then an open mouth. Babies babble them early, and parents happily treat them as words for mum and dad.

faq.q: Can babies learn two languages at once?
faq.a: Yes. Babies who hear two or more languages every day can grow up speaking all of them. Many children around the world do.

facts: Young babies can tell apart speech sounds from all languages, but by about 10 to 12 months they tune in mostly to the sounds they hear at home.
More than half of the world's people are thought to use two or more languages.
